title: System adjunction mates and normalized open maps respect shifts
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ work on the small pro-etale sites with $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ and the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_W$ (module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_W$ with compatible semilinear transition maps). Use its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$, total limit $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$, and actual adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ with unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. System operations are inverse image $P_v$ for separated finite-type maps $v$, direct image $S_p$ for proper $p$, quasi-compact open extension $J_j$, and derived tensor, with the integral counterparts of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Restrict input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs are derived complete and constructible. Use the fixed slotwise cochain shifts of [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data], with the signed second tensor slot, and the K-injective strict-tower Roos model for total limit. Write $\chi_H:H(M[r])\to H(M)[r]$ for a designated slot, holding other slots fixed. Use canonical simultaneous ringed-diagram-site models. Let $\mathcal G$ consist of the primitive comparisons of [lem-pur-system-primitive-comparison-shift], the units and counits of $P_v\dashv S_v$, $J_j\dashv P_j$ and $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$, and direct-image compositors (the conjugates of pullback compositors). Add the canonical normalized maps
$$\beta:P_gJ_j\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{j'}P_{g_U},\qquad \gamma:J_jM\otimes^LN\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j(M\otimes^LP_jN)$$
of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], for each cartesian open square $U'=U\times_X X'$ with $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $g:X'\to X$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $g_U:U'\to U$, with quasi-compact opens. The normalization is that $\beta^{-1}$ is the open adjunct of $P_{g_U}u_M$ followed by the inverse pullback compositor, and $\gamma^{-1}$ is the open adjunct of $u_M\otimes1$ through restriction/tensor comparison, where $u_M:M\to P_jJ_jM$ is the open unit.
Every map in $\mathcal G$, and these two normalized open maps and their inverses, commutes naturally with every integer shift in each input slot before evaluation of systems. More generally, for the listed adjunctions $F_a\dashv G_a$ with units $\eta_a$ and counits $\varepsilon_a$, a shift-compatible natural transformation $\alpha:F_2H\to TF_1$ has shift-compatible right mate
$$G_2(T\varepsilon_1)\circ G_2(\alpha G_1)\circ\eta_2HG_1:HG_1\to G_2T,$$
whenever $H,T$ have the fixed compatible shifts. The same holds for adjuncts $G(h)\eta$ and inverse isomorphisms. In the tensor cases the claim applies separately to either signed input slot. No proper/open interchange, projection or exchange square, or integral expression realization is included in this conclusion.

source.place: Agent-formulated obligation from the maps-used/coefficient-comparison sentences, adic transport Step 2; retained proof steps 6, 7 of lem-pur-integral-realization-shift-coherence (the blueprint itself does not assert the shift result)

proof.text: Use the simultaneous ringed-diagram models and actual system adjunctions of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Their operation shifts are precisely those fixed in [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data]: exact pullback and open extension use localized cochain shifts, proper image uses the adjunction mate, and reduction uses the mate of the total-limit shift. Apply [lem-pur-system-primitive-comparison-shift] to these models. It supplies every primitive comparison square in $\mathcal G$, in either designated tensor slot, intrinsically in the derived system category. In particular it supplies the pullback compositor and restriction/tensor squares needed below.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences; agent-expanded system shift argument, step 1

proof.text: For $P_v\dashv S_v$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] on the small simultaneous ringed diagram sites of step 1. Its canonical derived pullback is the stated exact system inverse image, and its right functor is total derived system direct image. Because system inverse image is exact, applying it termwise to a K-flat resolution $Q\to M$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $P_vQ\to P_vM$; with the resolution $Q[r]\to M[r]$ the K-flat shift comparison is therefore the termwise identity of $P_v$, that is, the localized cochain shift fixed for $P_v$. Its shift is the fixed adjunction-mate shift: uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] identifies it with the canonical K-injective comparison. Thus both unit and counit have their shift squares, including for the proper maps in the statement. For $J_j\dashv P_j$, both abelian system functors are exact and the adjunction is the localization of their specified degreewise adjunction. Apply [lem-pur-exact-adjunction-unit-shift-descent] to get the unit square for the fixed termwise comparisons; its degree-$m$ component at $M[r]$ is $u_{M^{m+r}}$, with differential $(-1)^r d$. Part (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] then gives the counit square for these same comparisons, without replacing the shift on $P_j$.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences; agent-expanded system shift argument, step 2

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-reduction-limit-shift-adjunction] with the given $R,t,W$ and the actual reconstruction calculus. It gives the unit and counit squares for $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ for every integer $r$, on the K-injective strict-tower total-limit model, including the shifted Roos-cone signs. By [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data], the total-limit shift here is this right-derived shift and the reduction shift is its adjunction mate, so these are the comparisons of the statement. No assertion about detecting equality after finite evaluation is involved.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences; agent-expanded system shift argument, step 3

proof.text: Fix any integer $r$. Apply the composition and both whiskering clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker], regarding its designated shift $[1]$ as the automorphism $[r]$. Thus composites of compatible transformations are compatible, with composite comparison $\chi_{BA,M}=\chi_{B,AM}\circ B(\chi_{A,M})$ in component notation. Inverses require only cancellation: from $\chi_B\tau_{M[r]}=\tau_M[r]\chi_A$, multiply by $\tau_M[r]^{-1}$ on the left and $\tau_{M[r]}^{-1}$ on the right to obtain $\chi_A\tau_{M[r]}^{-1}=\tau_M[r]^{-1}\chi_B$. The comparisons used here are natural isomorphisms, so all these cancellations are legitimate. These rules apply to the whole system derived categories, before any evaluation.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences; agent-expanded system shift argument, step 4

proof.text: For the general mate in the statement, form its three factors $\eta_2HG_1$, $G_2(\alpha G_1)$ and $G_2(T\varepsilon_1)$. The first and third commute with $[r]$ by the unit/counit squares of steps 2-3 and whiskering; the middle factor does by the hypothesis on $\alpha$ and whiskering. Step 4 composes these three squares: the two intermediate shift comparisons cancel, leaving exactly the shift square for $G_2(T\varepsilon_1)\circ G_2(\alpha G_1)\circ\eta_2HG_1$. For the adjunct $G(h)\circ\eta_X:X\to GY$ of $h:FX\to Y$, the identical two-factor calculation uses the square for $h$ (whiskered by $G$) and the unit square. For the other adjunct $\varepsilon_Y\circ F(h):FX\to Y$ of $h:X\to GY$, which is the form used in steps 7-8, it uses the square for $h$ whiskered by $F$ and the counit square of steps 2-3; again the intermediate comparison $F(\chi_G)$ cancels. This proves the claimed formulas for any of the listed adjunctions and fixed shift-compatible $H,T$.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences; agent-expanded system shift argument, step 5

proof.text: The direct-image compositors are the conjugates of the pullback compositors under the actual adjunctions, as stated in [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Apply step 5 to the pullback compositors of step 1. For a composite left functor its unit is the composite of the first unit with the first right adjoint applied to the second unit; its counit is the second counit composed with the second left adjoint applied to the first counit. Both are compatible by steps 2 and 4. Consequently the two successive adjunction transpositions defining each direct-image compositor are compatible, and so are inverse compositors by step 4. This proves the remaining compositor clause of $\mathcal G$.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences; agent-expanded system shift argument, step 6

proof.text: In the cartesian open square, write $\theta:P_{j'}P_g\cong P_{g_U}P_j$. The normalization in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], which explicitly also holds for strict inverse coefficient systems on ringed diagram sites, says $\beta_M^{-1}$ is the open adjunct of $h_M=\theta_{J_jM}^{-1}\circ P_{g_U}(u_M):P_{g_U}M\to P_{j'}P_gJ_jM$. The map $u$ has its square by step 2, and $\theta^{-1}$ has its square by step 1 and cancellation in step 4. Whiskering and composition give the square for $h$. Step 5 for $J_{j'}\dashv P_{j'}$ gives the square for $\beta^{-1}$, and step 4 gives that for $\beta$. Its isomorphism and its precise normalization are supplied by the cited node, rather than deduced from evaluations.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences; agent-expanded system shift argument, step 7

proof.text: Put $\rho:P_j(J_jM\otimes^LN)\cong P_jJ_jM\otimes^LP_jN$. By [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], $\gamma_{M,N}^{-1}$ is the $J_j\dashv P_j$-adjunct of $h_{M,N}=\rho^{-1}\circ(u_M\otimes1_{P_jN})$. Fix $N$ and shift $M$: the square for $u$ from step 2 and naturality of the first tensor-slot comparison give the square for $u_M\otimes1$; the square for $\rho^{-1}$ is the primitive restriction/tensor square of step 1. Now fix $M$ and shift $N$: naturality of the signed second-slot comparison gives the square for $u_M\otimes1_{P_jN}$, with the pullback shift on $P_jN$, and the same primitive square gives that for $\rho^{-1}$ in this slot. In each case step 4 gives the square for $h$ and step 5 gives that for its adjunct $\gamma^{-1}$. Inverting gives the square for $\gamma$. All morphisms have degree zero; the prescribed second-slot factor $(-1)^{ri}$ occurs on both sides of its naturality square, so no unsigned replacement is made.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences; agent-expanded system shift argument, step 8

proof.text: The preceding arguments use natural transformations and their natural shift comparisons, hence are natural in all inputs. The integer $r$ was arbitrary; the cited adjunction and primitive results cover zero and negative shifts as well. Fixing the other tensor argument in steps 4-5 gives precisely the designated-slot mate and adjunct arguments used in step 8. Every equality was obtained inside the original derived system categories, with the given normalized bounded domains used only for restriction of those functors; shifting changes the finite bounding intervals and retains their existence. This proves all stated clauses.
